summary: Andorra has no airport and no visa regime of its own — every visitor arrives by road through France or Spain, so Schengen rules decide who can come: EU/EEA citizens and Schengen visa-free nationalities enter freely, while travelers who need a Schengen visa must carry a double- or multiple-entry one, because entering Andorra means leaving the Schengen Area.

travelInsurance.text: Andorra does not require a visa. Travelers who need a Schengen visa to reach Andorra through France or Spain must hold the travel medical insurance the visa requires (minimum EUR 30,000 cover); winter-sports cover is strongly recommended for ski trips.

onwardTicket.text: Andorra requires no visa and is reached only through France or Spain, so the Schengen entry rules — including any request for proof of return or onward travel — apply when you first enter the Schengen Area.

source.name: Govern d'Andorra — Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Travel to Andorra

proofOfFunds.text: Andorra itself sets no requirement; France or Spain may apply standard Schengen means-of-subsistence checks when you enter the area.

source.name: Govern d'Andorra — Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Travel to Andorra

currencyLimits.text: Cash of EUR 10,000 or more must be declared to Spanish or French customs when you leave or re-enter the EU on the way to or from Andorra. No Andorran official source we could find states Andorra's own threshold.

source.name: Agencia Tributaria (Spanish Customs) — leaflet for travellers arriving from the Principality of Andorra

notes: Andorra is not in the EU. According to the UK FCDO, you may have to pay taxes and duties on tobacco, liquor and luxury goods when you re-enter France or Spain, and customs officers may impound excess tobacco and the vehicle carrying it.

payments.text: No official source we read describes card acceptance in Andorra. The Government of Canada states only that the currency is the euro (EUR).

safety.text: Street crime is rare, though you should still look after your belongings. Although Andorra has no recent history of terrorism, attacks cannot be ruled out. If you plan to ski, check the weather and avalanche safety advice before you go.

tips.text: If you needed a visa to enter the Schengen Area, the Government of Canada advises holding a multiple-entry visa before visiting Andorra: Andorra is outside Schengen, and holders of a single-entry visa may be refused re-entry to France or Spain.
Andorra is landlocked and has no airport, according to the Government of Canada; you must enter through France or Spain.
France and Spain apply strict limits on the tobacco and alcohol you bring out of Andorra for personal use. The UK FCDO says customs officers may impound excess tobacco and the vehicle carrying it.
From 1 November to 15 May you must use winter tyres or carry snow chains in Andorra, and you can be fined if you do not (UK FCDO).

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Andorra?
faq.answer: Andorra issues no visas at all. Entry is governed by Schengen rules because you must pass through France or Spain. EU/EEA citizens and Schengen visa-free nationalities (US, UK, Japan and many more) just drive in; if your passport needs a Schengen visa, get a double- or multiple-entry one so you can re-enter France or Spain afterward.

faq.question: Does time in Andorra count against my 90-day Schengen allowance?
faq.answer: No — Andorra is outside the Schengen Area, so days spent there are not Schengen days. If you plan to rely on that, keep evidence of your stay, such as hotel bookings and receipts.

faq.question: Can I visit Andorra on a single-entry Schengen visa?
faq.answer: You would be allowed into Andorra, but your single-entry visa would be used up — France and Spain can refuse to let you back into the Schengen Area, leaving you stranded. Only visit with a double- or multiple-entry Schengen visa or a residence permit.

faq.question: How do I get to Andorra without an airport?
faq.answer: By road, through France or Spain: Andorra has no airport (Government of Canada). From 1 November to 15 May, winter tyres or snow chains are compulsory on Andorran roads (UK FCDO).

faq.question: What currency does Andorra use?
faq.answer: The euro. According to the European Commission, Andorra is not in the euro area but has a monetary agreement with the EU that makes the euro its official currency.
